content: Clofibrate is a medication available under various trade names. In the United States, it is marketed as Atromid-S. In Canada, it is available as Atromid-S, Claripex, and Novofibrate. Warning: Clofibrate should only be used in specific patients after other treatments, including non-drug interventions, have failed to lower cholesterol levels. This is due to the potential for undesirable side effects. If you experience sharp abdominal or stomach pain, irregular heartbeat, chest pain, or notice any unusual growths (tumors), seek immediate medical attention. Uses: This medication is prescribed to reduce high cholesterol levels in the blood. How to Use: Clofibrate can be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. Do not increase your dose or stop taking the medication without consulting your doctor first. Side Effects: If you experience any of the following serious side effects, stop taking clofibrate and seek emergency medical attention: Allergic reactions, such as difficulty breathing, throat closure, swelling of the lips, tongue, or face, or hives. Chest pain or an irregular heartbeat. Severe stomach pain accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Fever, chills, sore throat, or flu-like symptoms. Blood in the urine or decreased urination. Swelling of the ankles or legs. Muscle cramps, weakness, aches, or pain. Joint pain. Sudden weight gain. Less serious side effects may also occur. Continue taking clofibrate and consult your doctor if you experience: Bloating or flatulence. Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Headache. Dizziness or drowsiness. Impotence. Other side effects not listed here may also occur. Report any unusual or bothersome side effects to your doctor. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you have any of the following conditions: Kidney disease. Liver disease. Gallbladder disease or gallstones. Heart disease. Ulcers. Any allergies. Clofibrate must not be used during pregnancy. Women of childbearing age should use reliable birth control methods while taking this medication. If pregnancy is planned, clofibrate should be discontinued several months before conception. This medication passes into breast milk and should not be used while breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Clofibrate may enhance the effects of certain drugs, potentially leading to dangerous side effects. These include: Anticoagulants (blood thinners) such as warfarin (Coumadin). Insulin or oral diabetes medications such as glipizide (Glucotrol), glyburide (Micronase, Diabeta, Glynase), tolbutamide (Orinase), or tolazamide (Tolinase). Clofibrate is generally not recommended for use with other cholesterol-lowering drugs, such as lovastatin (Mevacor), simvastatin (Zocor), pravastatin (Pravachol), atorvastatin (Lipitor), and gemfibrozil (Lopid). Combining these drugs can result in a serious reaction involving the muscles and kidneys, which may be fatal. Other drugs not listed here may also interact with clofibrate. Always consult your doctor and pharmacist before taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. Overdose: If an overdose is suspected, contact your local poison control center or emergency room immediately. U.S. residents can call the national poison hotline at 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents should contact their local poison control center directly. Notes: For optimal results, clofibrate should be used in conjunction with a low-fat, low-cholesterol diet. Follow any dietary recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Periodic laboratory tests will be conducted to monitor the effectiveness of this medication. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store clofibrate at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), away from heat and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Medication Appearance: Clofibrate is available by prescription under the brand name Atromid-S. It may also be available in other brand or generic formulations. Atromid-S 500 mg capsules are red, hard-gelatin capsules. Important Reminder: Keep this and all other medications out of the reach of children. Never share your medications with others, and use this medication only for the condition prescribed. Disclaimer: The information provided here is not intended to cover all possible uses, directions, precautions, warnings, drug interactions, allergic reactions, or adverse effects. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication.
